extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers interested in international affairs and diplomacy
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and publishing the final communique and resolutions of the 1955 Asian–African (Bandung) Conference, summarizing agreed principles, recommendations, and specific appeals on political, economic, cultural, and disarmament issues. Geared to inform the public about the conference's positions and calls to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for fundamental human rights and UN Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Full support of the fundamental principles of human rights as set forth in the Charter of the United Nations; note of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights as a common standard of achievement for all peoples and nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference declares full support and takes the UDHR as a common standard; underpins later recommendations on non-discrimination, self-determination, and education/cultural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of self-determination of peoples and nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Support of the principle of self-determination of peoples and nations as set forth in the UN Charter and relevant UN resolutions, declaring self-determination a prerequisite for full enjoyment of fundamental human rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for freedom and independence to be granted with the least possible delay to dependent peoples; used to justify appeals for Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco, West Irian, Palestine, Yemen, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of colonialism in all its manifestations
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare that colonialism in all its forms is an evil which should speedily be brought to an end and that subjection to alien subjugation, domination and exploitation is a denial of fundamental human rights and an impediment to world peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resolution avoided naming a single source (West vs. 'communist colonialism') but insisted on strong language condemning colonialism and calling upon powers concerned to grant freedom and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of racial segregation and racialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Deplore policies and practices of racial segregation and discrimination in large regions (explicit reference to South Africa) as gross violations of human rights and denial of fundamental values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express warm sympathy and support for victims, applaud those sustaining determination to eradicate racial discrimination; links racialism to cultural suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: States should respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core principle for friendly cooperation and a basis for non-interference and peaceful coexistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of equality of all races and nations, large and small
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand recognition of the equality of all races and the equality of all nations, large and small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms equality as a foundation of international relations and cooperation among Asian and African countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstention from intervention or interference in internal affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Call on all powers to abstain from intervention or interference in the internal affairs of another country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the conference's principles for peaceful coexistence and nonalignment; repeated as a core rule for inter-state conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: No collective pacts serving particular interests of big powers
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no collective pacts designed to serve the particular interests of any big powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against blocs or alliances that serve great-power self-interest rather than the collective good; tied to nonalignment rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstention from use of arrangements of collective defense to serve big-power interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstention from the use of arrangements of collective defense to serve the particular interests of any big powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that collective defense mechanisms should not be exploited for narrow great-power advantage; reinforces earlier prohibition on bloc-dominated pacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from acts or threats of aggression; peaceful settlement of disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from acts or threats of aggression or the use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any state; settle all international disputes by peaceful means such as negotiation, conciliation, arbitration or other peaceful means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes both prohibition of force and positive commitment to peaceful dispute resolution methods, in conformity with the UN Charter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect each nation's right to self-defense (singly or collectively) under the UN Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect for the right of each nation to defend itself singly or collectively in conformity with the UN Charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances non-aggression principles with recognition of lawful self-defense within UN rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstention from exerting pressures on other countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstention by any country from exerting pressures on other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition against political, economic, or other pressures meant to influence sovereign decisions of other states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of mutual interest and cooperation; respect for justice and international obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion of mutual interest and cooperation, and respect for justice and international obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General guiding principle intended to foster friendly cooperation, international peace and well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal admission to the United Nations where qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for universal membership in the United Nations and support for the admission of all states qualified for membership under the Charter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that universal UN membership is necessary for effective cooperation for world peace; specific participating countries named as deserving admission or representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable geographical distribution of Security Council representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expression of view that representation of Asian and African countries on the Security Council is inadequate and that distribution of non-permanent seats should reflect equitable geographical distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to increase the voice of Asian–African states in UN decision-making bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgency of economic development and promotion of economic cooperation respecting sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the urgency of economic development in the Asian–African region and desire for economic cooperation among participating countries on the basis of mutual interest and respect for national sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stresses that regional cooperation should not preclude cooperation with countries outside the region, including foreign capital investment where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance among participating countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating countries agreed to provide technical assistance to one another to the maximum extent practicable in the form of: experts, trainees, pilot projects and equipment for demonstration purposes, exchange of know-how, and establishment of national and regional training and research institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical mechanisms recommended for capacity-building and skills transfer, in cooperation with existing international agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations on international finance and development funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend early establishment of a special United Nations Fund for Economic Development; allocation by the IBRD of a greater part of its resources to Asian–African countries; establishment of international finance cooperation with activities including equity investment and encouragement of joint ventures among Asian–African countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks institutional and financial mechanisms to support development priorities and inter-regional investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizing commodity trade and adopting unified approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend collective action by participating countries for stabilizing international prices of and demand for primary commodities, and where practicable adopt a unified approach in UN advisory commission on international commodity trade and other international forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for cooperation to protect export earnings of primary-producing countries and coordination in international bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify exports and promote inter-regional trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Asian–African countries should diversify export trade by processing raw materials where economically feasible before export; promote inter-regional trade, exchange of trade delegations and business groups, exchange of information and samples, and provide facilities for transit trade of land-locked countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic development strategy emphasizing value-added processing, trade promotion, and practical support for landlocked economies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and remedy unreasonable shipping and transit rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that shipping lines have raised shipping rates often to the detriment of some countries; recommend study of the problem and inducement of shipping lines to adopt more reasonable attitudes; study of railway freight transit rates may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical suggestion to investigate transport cost barriers to trade and seek remedies through study and negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage national/regional banks and information exchange on oil issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement of national and regional banks and insurance; exchange of information on matters relating to oil such as remittance of profits and taxation might lead to formation of common policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks financial infrastructure and policy coordination to strengthen regional economic autonomy and bargaining power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote cultural cooperation and condemn cultural suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Convinced that cultural cooperation is a powerful means of promoting understanding among nations; condemn denial of basic cultural and educational rights under colonial rule and condemn cultural suppression, including racialism as a means of cultural suppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages renewal of historical cultural contacts, bilateral cultural exchanges, and policies to reverse colonial-era suppression of languages and cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational cooperation and exchange of students
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that better-placed Asian and African countries give facilities for admission of students from other Asian–African countries to their institutions; facilities should be available to those previously denied higher education opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates concrete student exchanges and access to higher education as part of cultural and technical cooperation; bilateral arrangements preferred for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote peaceful uses of atomic energy and proper representation in atomic agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize development of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes; welcome offers to make available information on peaceful atomic energy uses; urge speedy establishment of an International Atomic Energy Agency with adequate representation of Asian–African countries on its executive authority; recommend taking advantage of training and facilities offered by sponsoring countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine technology access, training, and institutional representation to ensure peaceful nuclear benefits for developing countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of liaison officers and fuller use of international organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to appoint liaison officers in participating countries for exchange of information and ideas; recommend fuller use of existing international organizations and that eligible participating countries secure membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative recommendation to improve information flow and leverage existing multilateral institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior consultation in international forums (not to form a regional bloc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend prior consultation of participating countries in international forums with a view to furthering mutual economic interest, while stating it is not intended to form a regional bloc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages coordination of positions but denies intent to create an antagonistic regional alliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for specific self-determination and dispute settlements (Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco, Palestine, West Irian, Indonesia–Netherlands, Yemen/Aden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations of support: rights of the people of Algeria and Tunisia to self-determination; support for Arab rights in Palestine and implementation of UN resolutions; support Indonesia in West Irian negotiations; support for Yemen in Aden and southern protectorates; urgent calls for peaceful settlement and reopening of negotiations where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political endorsements and calls to the concerned governments and to the UN to assist in finding peaceful solutions to these specific territorial/self-determination disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal for suspension of nuclear tests and experiments pending prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending total prohibition, the conference appeals to all powers concerned to reach agreement to suspend experiments with nuclear and thermonuclear weapons; disarmament and prohibition of manufacture, experimentation and use of such weapons are imperative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the conference in favor of immediate steps (test moratorium) as well as long-term universal disarmament and effective international control mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal disarmament as necessity for preservation of peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare that universal disarmament is an absolute necessity for the preservation of peace and request the United Nations to continue efforts to bring about regulation, limitation and reduction of armed forces and armaments, including prohibition of production, experimentation and use of weapons of mass destruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames disarmament as both moral responsibility and practical security necessity for humanity; calls for determined, speedy action and effective controls.
